items.stem: If claim counts follow a Poisson distribution, which statement is true?

options.rationale: Correct: for a Poisson distribution the mean and variance are both equal to the rate parameter.
A zero variance would mean a constant, not a Poisson count.
The Poisson distribution has a finite mean equal to its rate.

items.explanation: Correct: for a Poisson distribution the mean and variance are both equal to the rate parameter.

items.stem: An aggregate loss model S = X1 + ... + XN with N the claim count and X the severities assumes, in the collective risk model, that:

options.text: N and the severities are independent and severities are identically distributed
options.rationale: Correct: the collective risk model assumes independence of frequency and severity and i.i.d. severities.

options.text: Severities are always equal to the mean claim
options.rationale: Severities are random, not fixed at the mean.

options.text: The number of claims is fixed in advance
options.rationale: That is the individual risk model, not the collective model.
Severities are non-negative in standard loss models.

items.explanation: Correct: the collective risk model assumes independence of frequency and severity and i.i.d. severities.

items.stem: Select TWO quantities that increase as a deductible on a coverage increases, all else equal.

options.text: The insurer’s expected payment per loss decreases, so the retained loss to the policyholder increases
options.rationale: Correct: a higher deductible shifts more loss to the policyholder.

options.text: The expected number of payments the insurer makes (payments above the deductible) decreases
options.rationale: This decreases, not increases, so it is not a correct choice.
Correct: the retained loss below the deductible rises with the deductible.

options.text: The ground-up expected loss before any deductible
options.rationale: Ground-up loss does not depend on the deductible.

options.text: The insurer’s expected payment per loss
options.rationale: This decreases with a higher deductible.

items.explanation: Correct: a higher deductible shifts more loss to the policyholder.
